versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the software architecture and design are defined, properly implement the system/software requirements, and are safe. Standard: Computer system software architecture is defined. System level requirements are allocated to the subsystem and software requirements. All software and associated safety requirements are defined and allocated to software components. Software architecture is consistent with the software functional requirements; especially functions that ensure system integrity (e.g., partition schemes). The software architecture and design mechanizations implement proven techniques and are safe. The software architecture is compatible with the target hardware architecture. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, and inspection of documents. Inspection of software architecture design documentation ensures that the software architecture is defined. Analysis and test of the software architecture and design mechanization ensures software/system requirements are properly allocated, are met, and provide a safe implementation for the applications supported. Analysis ensures software design supports overall software architecture and does not conflict with system integrity requirements. References: JSSG-2008 Appendix A: 3.0 Computer Resources section (II.5.d); 3.1.5.1 gives guidance on data latency issues; 3.3.4 addresses synchronization, deterministic execution, and frame rate issues DoD JSSSEH: 4.3.3; 4.3.6.3.2; 4.3.7.1 USAF Weapon Systems Software Management Guidebook: F.4; Appendix I RTCA DO-178: For RTCA DO-178C: 5.0 and various subparagraphs; 6.0 and various subparagraphs including 6.3.3 Reviews and Analyses of Software Architecture; 11.7; 11.10 (see also DO-178B) IEEE 12207.0-1996 (s/s by ISO/IEC 12207:2008(E); IEEE Std 12007-2008): 5.3.5 software architectural design IEEE 12207.1-1997 (s/s by ISO/IEC 12207:2008(E); IEEE Std 12007-2008): 6.12 software architecture description ARINC Specification 653 FAA AC 20-115C

Standard: 1. Verify that the software architecture and design are defined, properly implement the system and software requirements, and are safe. Computer system software architecture is defined. System-level requirements are allocated to the subsystem and software requirements. All software and associated safety requirements are defined and allocated to software components. Software architecture is consistent with the software functional requirements; especially functions that ensure system integrity (e.g., partition schemes). The software architecture and design mechanizations implement proven techniques and are safe. The software architecture is compatible with the target hardware architecture. In addition, for designs utilizing MCP environments: 2. The software architecture implemented across the processing cores of an MCP is documented. 3. The software architecture accounts for the unique attributes associated with operation in the MCP environment. The software architectural design identifies: all cross-process and cross-processing core dependencies, within and external to, the MCP; processing scheme (e.g., AMP, symmetric multi-processing planned for each processing core; SESS allocation to processing cores (and VMs as applicable); MCP resource allocation to software architectural components; resource control and management (e.g., bus control software); hypervisor implementations; VMs utilized; partitioning schemes utilized; and the executive and control structure capability to support multicore operation to comprehensively show the software architecture’s interaction and operation with MCP hardware. 4. Any given instance of a process or processing task that is executing in a processing core (and VM as applicable) processing a SESS is assigned to only one processing core (and VM as applicable) and the assignment remains static during operation. The dynamic allocation of a SENSS process or processing task to a processing core or VM not processing a SESS does not adversely impact the integrity of SCF operation. 5. MCP resources needed for SESS operation are allocated and identified as shared or dedicated resources. 6. Single processing core SESSs that have been ported over for reuse on the MCP are identified and properly modified for use in the MCP environment. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): The number next to an MoC line item corresponds to the numbered line item in the standard that is being verified: 1. Verification methods include analysis, test, and examination of documents. Examination of software architecture design documentation ensures that the software architecture is defined. Analysis and test of the software architecture and design mechanization ensures software and system requirements are properly allocated, are met, and provide a safe implementation for the processes and processing tasks supported. Analysis ensures software design supports overall software architecture and does not conflict with system integrity requirements. In addition, for designs utilizing MCP environments: 2. Examination of software architecture design documentation ensures that the software architecture is defined. 3. Examination of software and MCP design documentation verifies that the software architecture accounts for operation within the MCP environment. Analysis verifies that the software architectural design accounts for the items identified in the standard and that the software architecture and hardware interaction and operation is fully understood. 4. Analysis of the software architecture within the MCP environment verifies that the assignments of process and processing task instances to a processing core (and VM as applicable) processing a SESS are appropriate and remain static during operation. Analysis and test verify that the dynamic allocation of a SENSS process or processing task to a processing core (and VM as applicable) not processing a SESS does not adversely impact the integrity of SCF operation. 5. Analysis verifies that MCP resources needed by each SESS are identified and designated as shared or dedicated. 6. Examination of software process documentation verifies that a sound approach was used to port single processing core SESSs to the MCP environment. Analysis of the SESS identifies the attributes that are accounted for to port to the MCP environment, or that no modifications are needed. Testing verifies that the function and performance of the ported software meets functional and performance requirements.
